name: 120bpm_alternating_8ths_triplets
description: Roadmap 1.4's own case. 120 BPM clicking quarters; the player plays a bar of straight eighths, then a bar of eighth-note triplets, then eighths again, for 16 bars. Neither grid is the other's, so every bar line is a change of feel the analyzer has to follow. It does not follow it: the inference locks on eighths in bar 0 and stays there for all sixteen, because a refractory keyed to eighths is 187 ms and a triplet arrives 166 ms after its neighbour, so two notes in five are never heard at all and the evidence a refit would need is exactly what was swallowed. The roadmap's two gates — 85 and two grid changes per eight bars — are both met anyway, which is what this fixture is really here to say: they can be met without following the player at all. See minHeardRatio.
